Worked Example: 170 lb, 30 Minutes

The formula is calories per minute = MET × 3.5 × body weight in kg ÷ 200. For a 170 lb person (about 77.1 kg) over 30 minutes, using commonly published MET values:

ActivityMETCalories in 30 min
Brisk walking (about 3.5 mph)4.3174
Cycling, moderate effort8.0324
Running (about 6 mph)9.8397

Why Your Watch May Disagree

MET-based estimates use averages. Fitness level, terrain, wind, heart rate and technique all change the real number, and devices differ in how they estimate it. Treat any figure as a rough guide, not a precise count.

Using the Result

  • Heavier people burn more for the same activity, so the figure rises with weight.
  • Do not treat exercise as a license to eat large amounts; the calories burned are often smaller than expected.
  • Combine this with your TDEE to see the larger picture.

extra_faqs.a: A MET, or metabolic equivalent, compares the energy cost of an activity with resting. One MET is the energy used sitting quietly, so a 4 MET activity uses about four times as much.

extra_faqs.q: Which burns more calories, running or walking?
extra_faqs.a: Running burns more per minute at the same body weight. Walking can still add up, since people can sustain it for longer.

extra_faqs.q: Does body weight change calories burned?
extra_faqs.a: Yes. A heavier person uses more energy for the same movement, so the same workout burns more calories.
